meta_description: A PipeWire mixer for Linux streamers: channels in rows, mixes in columns, a fader in every cell, effects per channel, and Stream Deck and Discord integrations.
og_description: The PipeWire mixer for Linux streamers.
hero_title: Your stream doesn't have to hear what you hear.
hero_lead: Pipedeck is a PipeWire mixer for Linux streamers, in the spirit of Elgato Wave Link. Send each application to a channel, then set how loud every channel is in each mix: your headphones, your stream and your call each get a balance of their own.
mixer_alt: The mixer: five channels in rows, three mixes in columns, a fader in each cell that links them.
features_title: A sound desk for everything that plays.
f_matrix_text: Channels in rows, mixes in columns, and a fader and a mute in every cell between them. Up to five mixes: Personal, Chat, Stream, Record and Aux.
f_apps_title: Apps go where you put them
f_apps_text: Attach an application to a channel once, and Pipedeck moves its sound there whenever it starts playing.
f_obs_text: Every mix is an input device named after it, so OBS, Discord or a browser list it with the microphones.
f_meters_text: Every channel, mix and cell shows what it passes on, as it plays.
f_keys_text: A level is the volume of its PipeWire node, so a media key or the desktop's volume applet moves the fader too.
f_restart_text: PipeWire or WirePlumber restarting? The mixer puts itself back together, and sends every application back to its channel.
f_monitor_text: Pick which mixes play in your headphones: your own, or the stream's for a moment to check what your viewers hear.
f_export_text: Export the whole mixer to a file, channels, mixes and effects, and import it on another computer or give it to a friend.
f_background_text: Close the window and the mixer carries on from the notification area, and starts with your session if you like.
how_title: Rows are what you play into. Columns are what you record.
channels_text: Where sound comes from: a virtual output any application can pick, or a microphone.
mixes_text: Where sound goes: an input device for OBS or a call, which can also play to your headphones.
cells_text: Link a channel to a mix, with that pair's own fader and mute. A cell exists only once you add it.
matrix_label: A small matrix: the microphone goes to the chat and stream mixes, music to all three at different levels, and the game to the personal and stream mixes.
effects_title: Treat a voice once, and every mix hears it.
e_denoise_text: takes fans, keyboards and hiss out from behind a voice.
e_eq_text: with five bands shaped for a voice, set by dragging them on a curve.
e_deesser_text: turns down harsh s sounds, and learns where yours are.
e_comp_text: evens out loud and quiet moments, set from five seconds of your voice.
effects_note: Built in, nothing to install. VST3 plug-ins and Thimeo's Stereo Tool run on a channel too.
eq_alt: The equaliser's window: five bands on a curve, over the zones a voice is talked about in.
integrations_title: On your Stream Deck, and in your calls.
sd_text: Mutes, levels, the mix in your headphones, effects and more on keys and dials, drawn the way the mixer draws them, meters and all. Through OpenDeck or StreamController, with ready-made layouts for the Stream Deck, Stream Deck + and XL.
discord_title: Discord, one voice at a time
discord_text: With Vesktop, a Discord call unfolds into a sub-track per person, each with a level and a mute of their own, remembered for the next call. Start a call and Pipedeck puts Vesktop on your voice chat channel by itself.
install_lead: Download a package from the latest release. Pipedeck needs GTK 4.18, libadwaita 1.7 and PipeWire 1.2 or later.
appimage_for: Other distributions with glibc 2.41 or later
